overview: Colonial Motor Company (CMC), founded in 1919 and NZX-listed since 1962, owns and operates a network of franchised motor-vehicle dealerships across New Zealand, anchored by 12 Ford dealerships (7 also carrying Mazda), alongside Southpac Trucks (Kenworth/DAF heavy trucks), Agricentre South (New Holland/Case IH tractors), JAC Motors, an expanding BYD electric-vehicle representation (via subsidiaries Energy Motors in Taranaki and the newly formed Adventure Motor Group in Canterbury/Wairarapa), and a range of other light-vehicle, motorcycle and parts/service franchises. A structurally important part of the business is CMC's large freehold property portfolio of dealership land and buildings, which it owns, develops and leases to its own operating subsidiaries at market rates, meaning a meaningful share of shareholder value sits in real estate rather than retail trading margin. The company is tightly held, with the Gibbons family (descendants of the founding family) collectively holding over 60% of shares, resulting in thin free float and low trading liquidity.

business_model.summary: CMC earns most of its revenue selling new and used vehicles, trucks and tractors through owned dealership subsidiaries, supplemented by parts, service and workshop revenue that acts as a profit ballast through the cycle, plus finance/insurance commissions on vehicle sales. Layered on top is an internal property business: CMC owns the freehold land and buildings under most of its dealerships and charges its own subsidiaries market rents, so consolidated results blend automotive retail margin with property income and periodic revaluation gains.

revenue_streams.name: Products (new & used vehicles, trucks, tractors, parts)
revenue_streams.trend: cyclical - recovering from FY2024/25 trough; H1-2026 Products revenue $504.3m vs $461.4m H1-2025 (+9.3%)

revenue_streams.name: Services (workshop, servicing, F&I-related)
revenue_streams.trend: growing steadily, more resilient than vehicle sales; H1-2026 $47.2m vs $45.5m H1-2025

revenue_streams.name: Other income (incl. property-related)
revenue_streams.trend: stable, plus periodic property fair-value gains recognised separately below the trading line

business_model.customer_type: B2C retail vehicle buyers plus B2B fleet, agribusiness and commercial trucking customers
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand only, but geographically diversified with a North Island Metro vs South Island/Rural split that management explicitly calls out as a 'two-speed economy' - North Island metro markets (Wellington, Auckland-area, Christchurch) have been weaker than South Island and rural/agribusiness-linked markets in FY2025-H1 2026

main_competitors: Andrew Simms/other independent Ford-Mazda dealer groups
Manheim/other truck importers for Southpac's Kenworth/DAF business
Chinese OEM-affiliated dealer networks (BYD, GWM, MG, Chery)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest Ford dealer groups in New Zealand (Ranger was the #1-selling vehicle nationally for 10 consecutive years through 2024, lost the top spot to the Toyota RAV4 in calendar 2025, then reclaimed #1 in the ute/commercial segment through H1 calendar 2026 and again in July 2026); niche leadership in Kenworth/DAF heavy trucks via Southpac and in New Holland/Case IH tractors via Agricentre South; now also a growing multi-region BYD dealer partner

moat_factors.description: Unlike many auto retailers that lease dealership sites, CMC owns much of its land and buildings (property, plant & equipment ~$258-284m carrying value, with a $117.6m property revaluation reserve embedded in equity as at Dec-2025), giving balance-sheet resilience, capital-appreciation upside and control over prime dealership real estate in growth corridors

Multi-decade Ford New Zealand relationships (dealerships since early-to-mid 20th century in several cases) and status as the largest single Ford dealer group provide scale in parts/service and negotiating position with the OEM, though the franchise itself is owned by Ford, not CMC

Spread across Ford/Mazda light vehicles, Kenworth/DAF trucks, agricultural equipment, JAC Motors and now BYD reduces reliance on any single brand or regional economy, evidenced by rural/agribusiness strength offsetting North Island metro weakness in FY2025 and by the June-2026 move to add a fast-growing Chinese EV brand to the portfolio
Services revenue has grown steadily (from $80.98m in FY2023 to $89.13m in FY2025, and to $47.2m in H1-2026 vs $45.5m in H1-2025) and is far less cyclical than new-vehicle sales, cushioning downturns

Gibbons family ownership >60% supports a multi-generational, conservative capital allocation approach (steady dividend policy, disciplined property investment) but also limits the influence of minority shareholders

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on Ford, and specifically the Ranger ute, for volume and profit - any Ford NZ model transition, allocation change or share loss (Ranger's 'sweet spot' commercial segment was down 18.4% in FY2025) directly hits earnings
Southpac's heavy-truck business is currently loss-making/weak amid falling national truck volumes and simultaneous Kenworth/DAF model transitions adding operational complexity
Thin free float and low share liquidity make the stock difficult for institutions to trade and can lead to persistent valuation discounts or premiums disconnected from fundamentals

Chinese EV/PHEV exposure is only now beginning (BYD representation via Energy Motors in Taranaki plus newly announced Adventure Motors BYD dealerships in Canterbury and Wairarapa from 30 June 2026), starting from a small base while BYD, GWM, MG and others have already taken >25% of some monthly passenger segments and the Shark 6 plug-in ute is eroding Ranger's light-commercial dominance
Low reported net margins (trading profit before tax of ~2.8% of revenue in FY2025) typical of vehicle distribution, leaving limited room to absorb further volume declines without cost actions

growth_drivers: Cyclical recovery in NZ new-vehicle registrations as the OCR falls - January 2026 registrations were up 8.9% YoY, the market was up 10.6% YTD through July 2026 (83,139 units), and H1-2026 trading profit after tax rose 50% YoY on stronger new and used vehicle sales
Refreshed group-wide focus on used-vehicle sales, which management credits as a key driver of the better-than-expected FY2025 and H1-2026 results
New model cycle at Ford - hybrid Ranger and Ranger Super Duty (arriving 2026, targeting the light-truck/heavy-fleet gap) expected to reinforce Ford's light-commercial dominance
Mazda's EV push (Mazda 6e and CX-6e battery-electric models arriving H2 2026) gives CMC's Mazda dealerships a new growth product as the brand transitions to BEVs

New BYD representation - CMC agreed with BYD Auto NZ (Ateco Group) on 30 June 2026 to expand its BYD footprint via subsidiaries Adventure Motor Group (new 'Adventure Motors BYD Canterbury' and 'Adventure Motors BYD Wairarapa' dealerships, with further locations flagged) alongside its existing Energy Motors BYD dealership in Taranaki, giving CMC direct participation in the fastest-growing segment of the NZ new-vehicle market rather than ceding it entirely to independent Chinese-brand networks

Ongoing property development programme - recent/current projects include the completed Fagan Motors (Masterton) rebuild, new Avon City Ford facility in Rangiora, land banked in Queenstown, a new Southpac facility in Palmerston North, and Hutchinson Motors' new Detroit Place facility in Christchurch - expanding capacity and adding to the freehold portfolio
New franchise wins - securing the Mitsubishi franchise in Manukau (May 2025, trading as Manukau Autos) and the BYD expansion (June 2026) show continued opportunistic franchise/dealership expansion

Southpac's growing Truck Related Parts (TRP) network (new stores in Nelson and Dunedin in H1-2026) extending the more resilient parts/service annuity into the truck segment even while new truck sales are weak

Agribusiness/dairy tailwind - strong dairy payout and improving red meat returns are driving a tractor-market recovery for Agricentre South after Kubota was divested (Nov 2025) to focus on core New Holland/Case IH franchises

business.description: Ford dealerships (12 of the group's ~19+ outlets) and the Ranger model in particular are central to group profitability; the light-commercial segment (Ranger's historical 'sweet spot') fell 18.4% in FY2025 even as Ranger regained the #1 ute/overall sales spot through July 2026
National truck volumes fell sharply in FY2025/H1-2026 outside dairy/agribusiness, compounded by Kenworth and DAF model transitions adding sales/marketing/inventory complexity

BYD, GWM, MG and other Chinese brands (8 brands combined) reached 26.2% of NZ passenger registrations in July 2026 (more than double their July 2025 share), and BYD's Shark 6 plug-in ute continues to take light-commercial share; CMC is now a BYD dealer partner itself (Energy Motors, Adventure Motor Group from June 2026) which mitigates but does not eliminate cannibalisation risk to its core Ford network
Prior years' commentary flagged high industry-wide inventory levels pressuring margins; excess stock has been a recurring theme through the downturn

financial.description: Vehicle floorplan finance of ~$79.9m (Dec-2025) plus current borrowings funds a large, low-margin inventory base ($221.5m at Dec-2025); a sharp demand drop can strand inventory and squeeze liquidity, as seen in the FY2024 operating cash outflow of -$40.98m driven by working-capital build

Interest expense fell from $15.5m (FY2024) to $14.2m (FY2025) and further to $5.4m in H1-2026 (vs $7.9m in H1-2025) as OCR cuts flowed through - the business benefits materially from rate declines and is correspondingly exposed if rates rise again
Management flagged a weak NZD as a potential H2-2026 headwind, given imported vehicles/parts are priced in foreign currency

regulatory.description: Although the Clean Car Discount feebate was repealed from 1 January 2024, the Clean Car Standard importer CO2 targets remain in force, requiring OEMs/importers to blend in more low-emission vehicles or pay penalties, which can affect model mix, pricing and availability

A prior Government decision to remove tax depreciation on commercial buildings drove a one-off non-cash deferred tax charge of $12.7m in FY2024 that crushed reported (non-trading) profit to $4.5m despite stable trading profit - illustrates how tax-policy changes on CMC's large property base can distort reported earnings without affecting cash flow

macro.risk: NZ consumer/business confidence and OCR path
macro.description: New-vehicle demand is highly correlated with interest rates and general economic conditions; management describes a 'two-speed economy' with weak North Island metro and truck markets versus resilient South Island/rural and agribusiness-linked demand, and cautioned that the strong H1-2026 trajectory 'may not be a realistic prospect' to sustain into H2

Agricentre South's tractor sales and part of the broader commercial vehicle base are geared to farm-gate returns; a downturn in dairy payout or red meat prices would remove a current offsetting tailwind
Heavy truck volumes are a leading indicator of broader freight/economic activity and remain depressed; management does not expect near-term momentum in this segment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The NZ new-vehicle market is in cyclical recovery: total registrations were up 10.6% YTD through July 2026 (83,139 units) with passenger volumes up 15.2%, though the July 2026 month itself was roughly flat overall as a 27.4% commercial-segment decline (against a tough Nissan Navara runout comparison a year earlier) offset a 14.5% passenger surge. Light commercial/ute demand remains the softer segment even as overall passenger volumes recover strongly, and heavy trucks and tractors lag the broader recovery.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - new-vehicle sales are strongly discretionary and rate-sensitive; CMC's own commentary explicitly frames FY2022-23 as a demand peak (aided by the Clean Car Discount feebate, repealed 1 Jan 2024) and FY2024-H1 2025 as the trough, with FY2025-H1 2026 showing recovery. Parts/service and property income are comparatively non-cyclical and provide earnings ballast
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - both directly (floorplan/vehicle finance funding costs) and indirectly (consumer/business willingness to finance vehicle, truck and tractor purchases); falling OCR through 2025-26 has been a clear tailwind to the H1-2026 result
key_input_costs: Imported vehicle costs (FX-exposed, NZD-denominated pricing on USD/JPY/EUR/RMB sourced product)
Staff remuneration (~$97.8m in FY2025, second-largest expense line after cost of products sold)

recent_developments.event: Agreed with BYD Auto NZ (a division of the Ateco Group) to expand BYD representation via subsidiary Adventure Motor Group Limited, establishing new dealerships 'Adventure Motors BYD Canterbury' (south Christchurch) and 'Adventure Motors BYD Wairarapa', with further locations flagged; complements the existing Energy Motors BYD dealership in Taranaki - CMC's clearest move yet to directly participate in the fast-growing Chinese-brand EV/PHEV segment rather than cede it entirely to independent operators
H1-2026 result: trading profit after tax of $10.4m, up 50.0% YoY, described as 'appreciably better' than anticipated at the November 2025 AGM; interim dividend held at 15.0cps, paid 30 March 2026

Market Guidance update on trading conditions issued to NZX; January 2026 new-vehicle registrations up 8.9% YoY, cited by the Board as early evidence of a sustained market recovery, though management cautioned that holding the H1 trajectory into H2 'may not be a realistic prospect'
Market Guidance update on trading conditions issued to NZX ahead of the H1-2026 result
Agricentre South sold its Kubota business (including the North Road, Invercargill property) to focus on core New Holland and Case IH heavy tractor franchises
2025 Annual Meeting held in Wellington; AGM resolutions passed, Chair's and CEO's addresses released to NZX

Hutchinson Motors opened a new leased facility on Detroit Place, Christchurch (replacing the St Asaph Street site), trading as 'Team Hutchinson All Makes' to expand used-vehicle and vehicle-prep capacity
Southpac Trucks opened two new Truck Related Parts (TRP) stores in Nelson and Dunedin, extending the more resilient parts/service network even as new heavy-truck sales remain subdued
FY2025 full-year result: trading profit after tax $17.8m (broadly flat vs FY2024's $17.9m) in a 'patchy' market; total FY2025 dividend held at 35.0cps (64% payout ratio), matching FY2024
Market Guidance update on trading conditions issued to NZX ahead of the FY2025 result
Secured the Mitsubishi franchise for Manukau, South Auckland, establishing 'Manukau Autos' on the Bakerfield Place site; Southern Autos relocated its hub to Botany Road as part of the change
Appointment of John Beveridge as an independent director

Completed the Fagan Motors (Masterton) dealership rebuild and brought the new Avon City Ford sales/service facility in Rangiora into operation; purchased further land adjacent to the Queenstown (Glenda Drive) dealership

Toyota RAV4 displaced Ford Ranger as NZ's best-selling vehicle for full calendar 2025, ending Ranger's 10-year run at #1, though Ranger regained the ute/overall lead through H1 calendar 2026 and again in July 2026 (738 registrations vs Toyota Hilux's 608)

Chinese OEM brands (BYD, GWM, MG, Chery, Zeekr, Jaecoo, Geely, Dongfeng) reached 26.2% of NZ passenger registrations in July 2026, more than double their July 2025 combined share, with BYD's Shark 6 plug-in ute (207 registrations in July) continuing to take share in the light-commercial segment CMC's Ford network has historically dominated

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 result (26 February 2026) and FY2025 result (21 August 2025)

items.target: Hold onto, if not build on, the gains of H1 FY2026
items.notes: Management explicitly said maintaining the H1 trajectory 'may not be a realistic prospect'; qualitative rather than numeric guidance, consistent with CMC's practice of not issuing formal earnings guidance. The Board periodically issues brief 'Market Guidance' NZX releases on trading conditions (e.g., 17-Dec-2025, 28-Jan-2026, 23-Jul-2025) rather than point-estimate earnings guidance.

items.target: Continued headwinds, no near-term recovery expected
items.notes: National truck volumes remain well down on prior year; management does not expect momentum to build in the short term despite Southpac 'performing well' relative to the tough market

items.target: Flagged as a risk to H2 FY2026 trading results
items.notes: Several vehicle model changes expected during 2026 (including Ranger Super Duty and Mazda 6e/CX-6e) could cause supply/demand disruption in the interim

items.target: Potential negative impact on trading results
items.notes: Called out alongside model-change disruption as a factor that 'both have the potential to impact trading results'

items.target: Interim 15.0cps declared for H1 FY2026 (unchanged for the third consecutive half)
items.notes: FY2025 full-year dividend was 35.0cps (64% of after-tax trading profit), matching FY2024; long track record of holding or growing the payout through the cycle

guidance.management_commentary: Chair A J Waugh described the FY2025 outcome as 'better than expected in a patchy market' and flagged a persistent 'two-speed economy' - weak North Island metro and truck markets versus resilient South Island/rural and agribusiness-linked demand. The H1-2026 letter noted the result was 'appreciably better' than anticipated at the November 2025 AGM, driven by a strong December, but was careful to frame this as partly a seasonal/fickle December effect rather than a certain trend, while welcoming the 8.9% YoY rise in January 2026 registrations as a positive early signal for the balance of the year. The 2026 Annual Meeting is scheduled for midday, Friday 6 November 2026, at the Harbourside Function Venue, Wellington.

bull_case: Business is emerging from a multi-year cyclical trough (H1-2026 trading profit after tax +50% YoY; FY2025 broadly stable despite a 'patchy' market) with OCR cuts and improving registrations (market up 10.6% YTD through July 2026) providing a tailwind into FY2026-27

Large owned freehold property portfolio (PP&E ~$258-284m, with a $117.6m property revaluation reserve embedded in equity) provides real, appreciating collateral value and downside protection largely absent from asset-light auto retailers, plus optionality to develop or realise sites

Resilient, growing parts/service (aftersales) revenue and a diversified franchise base (Ford/Mazda, Southpac trucks, Agricentre tractors, JAC Motors, Mitsubishi, and now BYD) reduce reliance on any single model cycle and smooth earnings through downturns

Proactive expansion into BYD dealerships (Adventure Motors BYD Canterbury/Wairarapa announced 30-Jun-2026, alongside existing Energy Motors BYD in Taranaki) gives CMC a direct stake in the fastest-growing part of the NZ vehicle market, partially hedging the risk that Chinese OEMs erode Ford's share

Long, consistent dividend history with a disciplined ~60-65% payout of trading profit after tax, funded by a business with modest net debt and strong long-term family ownership incentivised to protect the payout

Rural/agribusiness exposure (dairy payout recovery, red meat returns) is currently offsetting North Island metro weakness, giving the group a natural internal hedge that is playing out favourably right now
bear_case: Heavy dependence on Ford and the Ranger ute for profitability leaves CMC exposed as Chinese OEMs (BYD, GWM, MG and others, now 26.2% of passenger registrations in July 2026, more than double a year earlier) and Toyota erode share in exactly the light-commercial and passenger segments Ford has historically dominated; the new BYD dealership push is small-scale and unproven relative to the scale of this competitive threat to the core Ford business
Southpac's heavy-truck business remains structurally weak with no near-term recovery expected, and simultaneous Kenworth/DAF model transitions add cost and complexity risk

Thin free float (Gibbons family >60% ownership) means low liquidity, wide bid/ask spreads, and limited scope for index inclusion or institutional accumulation, which can keep the stock trading at a persistent discount to intrinsic/property-backed value regardless of fundamentals

Reported earnings can be volatile and non-representative of trading performance due to non-cash property fair-value and deferred-tax movements (e.g., the FY2024 $12.7m one-off deferred tax charge that cut reported profit to $4.5m against a stable $17.9m trading profit), complicating headline analysis for investors unfamiliar with the accounts

Management's own caution - flagging FX weakness, 2026 model-change disruption, and explicitly stating the strong H1-2026 trajectory 'may not be a realistic prospect' to sustain - suggests the recovery is fragile and dependent on continued OCR cuts and broader NZ economic improvement that is not guaranteed
